chunks: As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Hishām ibn Sālim, he said:

Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام was between Makkah and al-Madīnah, and Umm Ismāʿīl was with him. He had intercourse with a slave-girl of his, then instructed her, so she washed her body and left her head. He said to her: “When you want to ride, then wash your head.” She did that, and Umm Ismāʿīl came to know of it, so she shaved her head. Then when it was the following year, Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام came to that place, and Umm Ismāʿīl said to him: “What place is this?” He said to her: “The place in which Allah rendered your hajj of the previous year void.”

So this report is close to being one in which the narrator erred and did not preserve it accurately, and the matter became confused for him, because it is not impossible that he heard Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام say to her: “Wash your head, and when you want to ride, then wash your body,” but he narrated it in reverse. What indicates that is that the narrator of this report, namely Hishām ibn Sālim, narrated this very report exactly in the manner we have stated.

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام, the central authority in the report
key_terms.الرَّاوِي: the narrator whose precision is being evaluated
key_terms.الْخَبَرُ: the report or hadith under discussion
key_terms.بِالْعَكْسِ: in reverse, indicating reversal of the transmitted wording
key_terms.جَسَدَهَا: her body, referring to the bodily washing in ghusl
key_terms.حَجَّكِ: your hajj, mentioned as having been invalidated
key_terms.رَأْسَهَا: her head, referring to the head-washing mentioned in the report
key_terms.هِشَامُ بْنُ سَالِمٍ: the narrator cited as having transmitted the report in the correct form elsewhere

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith from al-Istibṣār indicate about the required order in ghusl al-janābah?
ai.summary: This report discusses the order of ghusl in the context of janābah and presents a narrative involving Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, Umm Ismāʿīl, and a slave-girl. The compiler then clarifies that the wording appears to have been reversed by a narrator, using another transmission from the same narrator to support the correct sequence.
